decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis best compares thirty-day staple-line leak between the separate groups, using the sparse table and assumptions in the exhibit?

answerChoices.label: Chi-square test of independence
answerChoices.rationale: The usual chi-square approximation is unreliable under the stated sparse expected counts. A two-by-two table does not by itself establish that approximation's adequacy.

answerChoices.label: McNemar test
answerChoices.rationale: McNemar testing concerns paired binary responses. The exhibit instead supplies separate participants or continuous matched differences, so that observation structure does not fit.

answerChoices.label: Paired t test
answerChoices.rationale: A paired t procedure needs repeated or deliberately matched measurements. This comparison does not supply those links between observations.

answerChoices.label: Fisher exact test
answerChoices.rationale: The exhibit supplies a sparse two-by-two table from separate participants. An exact categorical comparison fits the stated expected-count problem.
